text:
"Who would have thought that 'Kreider on the breakaway' would one day be a positive for Canadiens fans?" Karine Hains of The Hockey News asked it after Chris Kreider scored on one against Pittsburgh, and it sums up his first month in Montreal: a 35-year-old former Ranger scoring in a lineup that's playing without Nick Suzuki.

He has nine points in 17 games in under 14 minutes a night, and CBS Sports called it a warming trend. The scoring is honest (three goals on 3.4 expected, the quality of his chances). The warning sign is the chance share: Montreal has only 42% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, 14 points worse than without him, and has scored 6.2 more goals than expected when he's out there. His ice time is down almost two and a half minutes over the last ten games.

He scored 348 goals before this season, 883 games as a Ranger. Our projection sees about 15 goals from here. The finish is still there; the legs are the question.
